unit: Students can describe their daily study routines, discuss learning tools, and share advice for building good study habits while balancing school and family life.
lesson: Lesson 4: A Good Place to Study
objective: Describe a quiet and comfortable study space at home.

title: Warm-up
subtitle: Finding a comfortable place at home
question: Where do you usually sit when you read or study at home?
starters: My favorite place to read is...

title: Useful Language (Part 1)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat it.
Read the definition and the example sentence.
Ask the check question to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: making very little or no noise
words.example: I need a quiet place to read my book.
words.check: Which place is usually quiet: a library or a market?

words.definition: making a lot of loud noise
words.example: The classroom gets noisy when the students are talking.
words.check: Which place is usually noisy: a busy road or an empty park?

title: Useful Language (Part 2)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat after you.
Read the definitions and example sentences.
Ask the check questions to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: Making your body feel relaxed and free from pain.
words.example: I sit in a comfortable chair when I study.
words.check: Which is more comfortable: a soft sofa or a hard wooden chair?

words.definition: A table that you sit at to write, study, or work.
words.example: I keep my computer and books on my desk.
words.check: What do you usually keep on your desk?

words.definition: Filled with a lot of light.
words.example: The room is bright because it has large windows.
words.check: Which is brighter: a room with large windows or a room with no windows?

title: Conversation Builder
goal: Learn how to talk about your favorite place to study.

linkers.use: Say where you sit, such as at a desk.
Explain why this place is good.

model:
Tutor: So, where do you usually study at home?
Student: Well, I prefer to study in my bedroom. I like studying at my desk because it's comfortable.
Tutor: That sounds nice. Is it quiet in your bedroom?
Student: Yes, it's bright and quiet. It is better to study there because it isn't noisy.

your_turn.teacher: Ask the student where they study at home. Then, ask if their space is noisy or bright.
your_turn.student: Answer the tutor. Describe your study space using the new phrases.

title: Let's practice
teacher_question: Imagine you need to read your textbook at home. Tell me about your favorite room to study in. You can choose the living room, your bedroom, or the kitchen. Use the phrases below to describe if it is quiet, comfortable, or bright.
student_guide: I prefer to study in the ___ because it is ___.
I like studying in my ___ because it is very ___.
It's a great place to study, but sometimes it gets too ___.

title: Real-world scenario
role_a: You are the student. Describe your favorite place to study at home.
role_b: You are the tutor. Ask the student if their study space is too noisy or if it's bright enough.
problem: You need to find the best place to open your textbook and focus.
mission: Tell the tutor where you like to study.
Use words like quiet, comfortable, and desk.
Answer the tutor's questions about noise and light.
start: Tutor: So, tell me, where do you prefer to study at home?

title: Wrap-Up
recap: Vocabulary: quiet, noisy, comfortable, desk, bright
Chunks: I prefer to study in... / I like studying at... / It is better to...
Skill: Describe a quiet and comfortable study space at home.
final_task: Use one of today's chunks to answer this question in one sentence: Where is your favorite place to study at home?
challenge: Before your next class, organize your desk to make it a more comfortable place to study.
